item.title: Let's Watch (Guild Room) — Fri Nov 6, 6:00 PM — Guild Room
item.description: A Most Beautiful Thing (2020, 1h35) follows the story of the first African American public high school rowing team in the United States. Formed in the 1990s at Manley High School and based in Chicago’s West Side, the team was made up of young men, many of whom were members of rival gangs. Reuniting after 20 years, the team gets back on the water to prepare to race in the 2019 Chicago Sprints, the largest rowing regatta in the Midwest. In the process, Arshay Cooper, the team’s captain, takes inspiration from the past and reaches out to the Chicago Police Department to show that rowing can bring even people with the most disparate of backgrounds together. A MOST BEAUTIFUL THING explores not only the safety these young men found on the water (where, as the captain reflected, “we were in a place where we could not hear the sound of sirens”), but the trauma of violence and cyclical poverty, examining how these young men were able to support each other in reimagining a different future fo

item.title: 🚶Yanticaw Park Nutley — Sat Nov 7, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! Meet along Park Drive in Nutley near the Orechio Sports Complex. We'll walk about 3.5 mile through scenic Yanticaw Park, up to Kingsland St. and back. The path is paved and mostly flat.
Please check the event page beforehand in case of any changes. Inclement weather will cancel the walk.
The Yanticaw Park is an Essex County-owned park in Nutley, New Jersey. It is located between Centre Street and Chestnut Street, extending west to Passaic Avenue.
Essex County began purchasing land in 1911 for creation of the park. Wetlands in the park were drained, and a dam was set up to form a lake. The park was completed in 1914. In 1962, the lake, containing a small island was drained and a channel was dug as a continuation of the natural third river from the south.
PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES **EARLY** SO WE CAN START TO WALK ON TIME

item.description: 50 years ago, on Thanksgiving night in 1976, Americana Rock pioneers The Band would take the stage for what would be their final concert. Captured by film director Martin Scorsese, this enormous occurrence would be witnessed, captured, & shared world wide for over 5 decades. Since that day when the film debut, professional musicians & lovers of this concert would recreate it for both artistic or even charitable significance. Since 2023, ROSTAFA & CO. have brought this one of a kind Thanksgiving tradition to the town of Montclair to help those in need during the holiday season. Raising over $15,000, this event has become the biggest concert fundraiser of the entire year. North NJ musicians, including those from Montclair, recreate the magic & brilliance of a timeless classic of honor American music that shaped the 20th Century & beyond. item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Sat Nov 7, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. ⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.
🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort.
